title: Supreme Court issues notice, refuses interim stay in Shiv Sena (UBT) challenge to Lok Sabha Speaker’s merger recognition of rebel MPs
summary: The court has taken up the anti-defection dispute over six rebel MPs’ merger with the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena but has not ruled on the merits yet; the case returns after two weeks.

claims.text: The underlying dispute concerns disqualification proceedings involving rebel Shiv Sena MPs and the Lok Sabha Speaker’s office.
The constitutional issue appears to be the timing and handling of disqualification petitions under the anti-defection framework.
The Supreme Court is reportedly being drawn into a review of, or pressure on, the Speaker’s discretion or delay.
If the Court does engage, the case could create a precedent on judicial oversight of Speaker inaction in defection disputes.
The dispute may affect the MPs’ legislative status and the Speaker’s practical discretion, but the exact legal effect is unverified here.

In this run, the Supreme Court material located for the Shiv Sena UBT merger dispute shows a notice stage only: the bench issued notice, sought responses from the Lok Sabha Speaker and other respondents, and listed the matter for later hearing.
